mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons alongside a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deterioration in labor market quality despite headline employment growth, which reduces corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 AND UNRATE monthly change > 0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month INDPRO declines below -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which reduces household wealth and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during four-month HOUST < 1,200,000 episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, in conjunction with a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4%, signals aggressive monetary tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.33% (4% annualized)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS jumps >0.75% and CPIAUCSL >4% YoY in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during six-month stretches of UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 4% combined with a positive year-over-year change in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 2% signals robust aggregate demand growth, which expands corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY > 4% and PAYEMS YoY > 2%.
